# Visual reference map

Choose images by the rule being applied. Inspect the relevant full painting
before its detail crop, then supply those images to the image tool with their
roles stated explicitly. Do not send every asset as an undifferentiated style
set. These references support original compositions, not tracing.

## Corrections override older pictures

The original paintings demonstrate composition, shared shapes, depth, and
subject-related context. The generated head sheet demonstrates approved feature
economy; the accepted pose demonstrates a particular head-neck relationship.
Neither generated image replaces the originals for rules it does not show.

Preserve the user's later refinements even when an older reference differs:

- One clear eye is the default; a second is optional unless an exact count is
  required. The actual eye opening follows the head, not just its color patch.
- For the refined sideways treatment, long loose hair falls downward from
  head-led roots; leave the image-top-facing head edge exposed without a cap.
- Preserve a fuller cheek and softly offset chin, not a needle point.
- Omit the long hair-side-to-nose line. Keep nose and mouth marks selective
  and independently displaced rather than restoring conventional anatomy.

Rejected swan-neck, animal-muzzle, repeated eye-symbol, and conventional-portrait
tests are not generation references. The user requested the final
paintings as learning assets; their inclusion does not approve every detail.
Use only the relationships identified in their learning entries, especially
where conventional facial construction remains a limitation. Do not add a new
generated scene to the set without the user's request or acceptance.
Personal photographs are loose topic guides, not style assets or redraw targets. Follow the
[photo-reference workflow](style-guide.md#photographs-as-loose-topic-guides):
extract subjects, activity, and broad positions, then compose using the artwork
references. Omit the photo from image-tool inputs when that brief is sufficient.

## Source and crop provenance

`assets/final-paintings/` contains unchanged generated scene images.
The NYC dancers and blue-eyed drummer are the user's selected uploads of those
results; the other images are the retained scene outputs. They are not source
paintings, personal photographs, or crops of the original artwork.

[The complete supplied reproduction](../assets/source-paintings.png) preserves
the two separate paintings side by side, including existing text and visible
reproduction marks. It is not a diptych or a clean scan of either painting.
`family-handoff.png` preserves the user's separately supplied close-up unchanged.
The other source details are unretouched rectangular crops of the complete
1408 by 1015 reproduction:

| Crop | Bounds in source pixels: left, top, right, bottom |
| --- | --- |
| `source-drummer.png` | `0, 0, 710, 1015` |
| `source-family.png` | `725, 0, 1408, 1015` |
| `family-merged-profiles.png` | `855, 0, 1275, 450` |
| `drummer-depth.png` | `0, 140, 710, 1015` |
| `typography-family.png` | `725, 0, 1408, 150` |
| `typography-drummer.png` | `0, 0, 320, 110` |

Right and bottom bounds are exclusive. Crops isolate details; they do not
reconstruct content missing from the supplied image. Do not erase watermarks,
infer an artist or license, or reproduce source lettering as new artwork.
Bundling user-supplied references is not a grant of redistribution rights;
confirm permission before publishing or sharing them with the skill.
